summary: Comprehensive pytest suite for the new Bid backend feature: 17 tests across create/update, validation, deviation, check, listing-view, counts and withdraw. All 17 tests pass against the local backend at http://localhost:8001.

minor.issue: On update, the returned response carries the bidder profile (bidder_name/bidder_company) taken from the LATEST users lookup, but on an update the bidder profile in the DB is also overwritten via $set bid_doc. This is consistent — just noting that resubmitting a bid will refresh the cached bidder_name/bidder_company even if the bidder didn't change them. Not a bug, just a behaviour to document.

When viewer_phone is malformed (not 10 digits) it returns {bid_placed:false} silently with HTTP 200 instead of 400. Consistent with GET /api/bids/counts/{phone} which also returns {} for malformed phones — fine for a public read endpoint but worth documenting.
Returns 404 if the bid was never placed (or already withdrawn). Frontend should treat 404 on withdraw as 'already gone' rather than surfacing an error to the user.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1962 lines — strongly consider splitting bids/PTL/loads/users into separate routers/modules. File-size guideline (>700 lines) is well exceeded.

Bid endpoints currently rely on viewer_phone passed as a query param for authorization (owner-only access to /api/bids/listing/{id}). There is no token verification — anyone who knows the poster's phone number can list their bids. Acceptable for an internal MVP but should be hardened (use /api/auth/verify-token like other endpoints).
BidCreate.weight_tons has no upper bound; consider validating against TRUCK_CAPACITY_KG / a sane max so bidders cannot submit absurd values.

POST /api/bids does not require listing_type to actually match where the listing lives — if a caller sends listing_type='load' but the id is a PTL id, _get_listing returns None and the call 404s (good). However a caller could send listing_type='ptl' for a real load id and the listing would not be found. The endpoint already behaves correctly, but a clearer error message like 'listing not found in <listing_type> collection' would help debugging.

Indexes on db.bids are created lazily on startup. Safe — but the unique compound index (listing_id, bidder_phone) means any race on first-create will collide with the existing update branch. Current code handles this by check-then-update; under high concurrency a brief race window exists where two inserts could both happen. Consider using upsert with $setOnInsert for atomicity.

bidder_name/bidder_company are denormalised onto the bid at write time. If the bidder later updates their profile, the bid still shows the OLD name/company. Acceptable, but should be a product decision (denormalise vs join-on-read).
test_credentials: None required — Bid APIs are unauthenticated. Test users are created on the fly with random 10-digit phones (TEST_Poster, TEST_Bidder, TEST_Bidder2).
seed_data_creation: Tests create their own fresh users, loads and a PTL load per module run, all suffixed/named with TEST_. No global seed required. MongoDB will retain these documents after the run; consider periodic cleanup of TEST_-prefixed records.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 17 bid tests pass against http://localhost:8001. The prod backend (https://ptl-market.onrender.com/api) does NOT yet have these endpoints — do not test against it. To re-run: `python -m pytest /app/backend/tests/test_bids_api.py -v`. Coverage matrix maps 1:1 to the 13 scenarios in the original review request. Note that server.py is now very large (~2k lines) and a refactor was flagged for the main agent.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Feature works end-to-end as specified.
